record.original_question: Let ∞ X f (z) = an z λn n=0 be analytic in D and have Hadamard gaps, i.e. λn+1 /λn ≥ q > 1. Need f have any radial limits (finite or infinite)? If not, need f have any asymptotic value on a path ending at a single point? For the case q ≥ 3, see MacLane [547]. (J. M. Anderson and R. Hornblower)

evidence.quote: Let ∞ X f (z) = an z λn n=0 be analytic in D and have Hadamard gaps, i.e. λn+1 /λn ≥ q > 1. Need f have any radial limits (finite or infinite)? If not, need f have any asymptotic value on a path ending at a single point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. Suppose
$$f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^{\lambda_n}$$
is analytic in $\mathbb{D}$, where $(\lambda_n)_{n\ge 0}$ is a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative integers satisfying the Hadamard gap condition
$$\frac{\lambda_{n+1}}{\lambda_n}\ge q>1\qquad\text{for all }n\ge 0.$$

Recall that:
- A radial limit of $f$ at $e^{i\theta}\in\partial\mathbb{D}$ is the limit (finite or $=\infty$) of $f(re^{i\theta})$ as $r\to 1^-$, when it exists in $\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$.
- An asymptotic value of $f$ at a boundary point $\zeta\in\partial\mathbb{D}$ is a value $w\in\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that there exists a continuous path $\gamma:[0,1)\to\mathbb{D}$ with $\gamma(t)\to\zeta$ as $t\to 1^-$ and $f(\gamma(t))\to w$.

Answer the following:

(a) Must $f$ possess at least one radial limit (finite or infinite) at some point of $\partial\mathbb{D}$?

(b) If the answer to (a) is negative, must $f$ at least possess an asymptotic value along some path in $\mathbb{D}$ ending at a single boundary point of $\mathbb{D}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Classical results of MacLane handle the case $q\ge 3$, and Binmore–Hornblower (Nagoya Math. J. 48, 1972) treated large $q$ and the case of arbitrary $q>1$ under the additional hypothesis $a_n\to 0$, showing such $f$ lies in MacLane's class (and hence has asymptotic values). For general $q>1$ without coefficient decay, no resolution was found in the search; the problem appears to remain not fully settled in the literature located.

status_evidence.title: Boundary behaviour of functions with Hadamard gaps (Binmore–Hornblower)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper studying when Hadamard gap series belong to MacLane's class; results include large q and arbitrary q>1 when coefficients tend to zero.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known: MacLane for q≥3; Binmore–Hornblower for large q and for q>1 with a_n→0.

status_evidence.title: Ostrowski–Hadamard gap theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Power series with Hadamard gaps cannot be analytically continued past the boundary of the disc of convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on Hadamard gap series.
